title: Golden Monkey Trekking in Rwanda: Permits, Costs and What to Expect
meta_title: Golden Monkey Trekking in Rwanda: 7 Essential Tips
meta_description: Golden monkey trekking in Rwanda: US$100 permits, age rules, what happens on the day, best months and costs from Kigali. Plan your Volcanoes trip.
excerpt: Everything you need for golden monkey trekking in Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park: verified permit rates, the 07:00 start at Kinigi, the best season, realistic costs and how to pair it with gorillas.
content:
Golden monkey trekking in Rwanda is a guided walk into the bamboo forest of Volcanoes National Park to spend about an hour with a habituated troop of endangered golden monkeys. Treks start at 07:00 from Kinigi park headquarters, the permit costs US$100 for foreign adults (checked October 2026), and the minimum age is 12.

Most travellers hear about golden monkeys as an add-on to gorillas, then wonder whether the extra day is worth it, how hard the walk is and how to fit it into a tight Rwanda schedule. This guide covers the permit rates for every visitor category, what happens on the day, the best season, realistic trip costs and how to pair the monkeys with gorillas, Mount Bisoke or a Kenya safari.

Quick Facts

  • Where: Volcanoes National Park, Musanze District, north-west Rwanda, about 2.5 hours by road from Kigali
  • Permit: US$100 per foreign adult; lower rates for residents and East African citizens (checked October 2026 on the RDB booking portal)
  • Minimum age: 12 years
  • Start: report at 07:00 to Kinigi park headquarters for the briefing
  • Time with the monkeys: about one hour once the troop is found
  • Group size: up to 16 visitors per golden monkey group
  • Best season: the drier months of June to September and December to February

What Is Golden Monkey Trekking in Rwanda?

Golden monkey trekking in Rwanda is a ranger-led visit to one of two habituated golden monkey troops in Volcanoes National Park. You walk through farmland and into the bamboo zone, find the troop with your guide, then watch and photograph the monkeys for about an hour before walking back.

Golden monkeys are a bright orange and black form of the blue monkey, known scientifically as Cercopithecus mitis kandti (some authorities treat it as a full species, Cercopithecus kandti). They live only in the highland forests of the Albertine Rift, mainly the Virunga volcanoes shared by Rwanda, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo. The IUCN Red List classes them as Endangered in its 2020 assessment, so every permit helps fund their protection.

Bamboo is the food golden monkeys eat most often, because it is available all year in the Virungas. That is why treks focus on the bamboo belt on the lower volcano slopes. Troops can hold up to 30 animals, and they are fast, playful and constantly on the move, which makes the hour very different from the calm of a gorilla visit.

Where do you see golden monkeys in Rwanda?

Volcanoes National Park has two groups open to visitors, according to Visit Rwanda: one on the slopes of Mount Karisimbi and one in the bamboo forest on Mount Sabyinyo. Golden monkeys also live in Gishwati Forest in western Rwanda, but Volcanoes is where almost every traveller tracks them, and the official tracking departs once a day from Kinigi.

How Much Does Golden Monkey Trekking Cost?

Golden monkey trekking costs US$100 per foreign adult for the permit (checked October 2026 on the Rwanda Development Board booking portal). Residents and East African citizens pay less. The permit is the smallest part of the bill: transport from Kigali and a night near the park usually cost more.

Rates are from the official RDB golden monkey booking page (checked October 2026). Resident rates need at least four consecutive months of residency or a work permit, and East African rates need an EAC ID card or passport. Permit prices can change, so confirm the current rate before you book.

Most travellers do not make a separate trip for golden monkeys. Adding the trek to a gorilla itinerary usually costs only the permit plus one extra night, because the vehicle and guide are already there. What Happens on a Golden Monkey Trekking Day?

A golden monkey day starts early, with a 07:00 briefing at Kinigi and a short drive to the trailhead, and usually ends by lunchtime. The rhythm is simple: briefing, walk in, one hour with the troop, walk out.

Briefing at Kinigi park headquarters

Kinigi is the starting point for gorillas, golden monkeys and the volcano hikes. Rangers check permits and passports against your booking, so the names and document numbers you gave at booking must match. Visitors are then split into groups, and your guide explains the rules, the troop you will visit and the route.

The walk into the bamboo

From the trailhead you cross cultivated fields to the park boundary wall, then enter the bamboo forest to find the troop. The walk is usually shorter and gentler than most gorilla treks, but the length depends on where the monkeys moved overnight, and the ground can be muddy and slippery, especially after rain.

One hour with the troop

Once you reach the monkeys, the hour starts. Golden monkeys leap between bamboo stems, feed on shoots and leaves, groom each other and chase through the canopy. They move quickly and the forest is dim, so photographers should be ready with a fast shutter speed. Your guide will ask you to keep your distance, stay quiet and avoid flash.

Is Golden Monkey Trekking Hard?

Golden monkey trekking is one of the easier primate activities in East Africa. Anyone with moderate fitness who can walk for a couple of hours on uneven, muddy ground should manage it. The altitude in the Virungas is high, so walk at a steady pace and drink plenty of water.

Compared with gorilla trekking, there is less climbing and the minimum age is lower, at 12 rather than 15 for gorillas, which makes the monkeys a good option for families with younger teenagers. Porters from the surrounding communities can be hired at the trailhead to carry your daypack and help you on slippery sections.

What should you wear for golden monkey trekking in Rwanda?

Wear long trousers tucked into your socks, a long-sleeved shirt and broken-in waterproof hiking boots, because bamboo and nettles scratch and the trail is often wet. Bring a rain jacket, gardening gloves for gripping vegetation, a small daypack with water and snacks, and a camera with spare batteries. Mornings in the Virungas are cool, so a light fleece helps.

When Is the Best Time for Golden Monkey Trekking?

The best time for golden monkey trekking is during Rwanda's drier months, June to September and December to February. Trails are firmer, light is better for photos and walking is easier. Treks run all year, though, and the monkeys stay in the bamboo zone whatever the season.

The rainy months, roughly March to May and October to November, bring muddier trails and more cloud, but also greener forest and quieter lodges. Golden monkey permits are far easier to secure than gorilla permits, yet groups are capped at 16 visitors, so book a few weeks ahead in the peak months of July and August.

How to Plan Golden Monkey Trekking in Rwanda

Planning this trip comes down to three choices: how you combine it with other activities, where you sleep and how you get to Kinigi. Most visitors fly into Kigali, drive about 2.5 hours north to Musanze or Kinigi and stay one to three nights near the park.

Golden monkeys with gorillas

The classic pairing is a gorilla trek on one day and golden monkeys the next morning, then the drive back to Kigali. Our 2-day gorilla and golden monkey trekking trip follows exactly that plan, with the gorilla and golden monkey permits, a private 4x4 and full-board accommodation near the park.

Golden monkeys without a gorilla permit

Golden monkey trekking is also a lower-cost way to experience the Virungas if the gorilla permit is outside your budget or your children are under 15. The 3-day golden monkey trekking and Mount Bisoke hike pairs the monkeys with a climb to Bisoke's crater lake at 3,711 metres, plus a Kigali city tour.

Combining Rwanda with Uganda or Kenya

Golden monkeys also live across the border in Uganda's Mgahinga Gorilla National Park, which features in our guide to the best national parks to visit in Uganda. Kigali also has direct flights to Nairobi if you want to add the savannah, and a Kenya safari in January pairs well with a Rwanda primate trip in the short dry season.

Golden Monkey Trekking or Gorilla Trekking: Which Should You Choose?

Golden monkey trekking and gorilla trekking are very different experiences, and if your budget allows, doing both is the best answer. Gorillas are the once-in-a-lifetime encounter; golden monkeys are the lively, affordable second day that rounds out a Volcanoes visit.

Minimum age1215
Visitors per groupUp to 16Up to 8
EffortUsually easier, bamboo zoneCan be steep and long
The encounterFast, playful, in the canopyCalm, close, on the ground

Permit prices were checked in October 2026 on the RDB booking portal. If you can only do one, choose gorillas for the emotional impact and golden monkeys if budget, age or fitness rules gorillas out.

Insider Tips

  • Match your documents: book with the exact passport details you will carry, because RDB checks them at Kinigi and errors can mean refused entry
  • Leave early: from Kigali you need to set off around 04:30 to reach Kinigi for 07:00, so most travellers sleep near the park the night before
  • Set your camera first: use a high ISO and fast shutter speed before you start, as the monkeys move quickly in dim bamboo
  • Hire a porter: it makes muddy sections easier and supports local families
  • Pack gloves: cheap gardening gloves help when you grab bamboo or nettles on the slope
  • Insure the trip: choose cover that includes hiking and medical evacuation, such as our travel insurance options

Rules and Responsible Golden Monkey Trekking

Responsible trekking means following your ranger's instructions on distance, noise and behaviour. Golden monkeys are endangered and habituated for tourism only under strict conditions, so the rules protect them from stress and disease.

Keep the distance your guide sets, never feed or touch the monkeys and do not eat near them. Switch off your flash, keep voices low and stay with your group. If you have a cold, cough or other illness, tell the rangers: primates catch many human infections. For a wider picture of Rwanda's primate experiences, see the official Visit Rwanda primate tracking page. Check the yellow fever requirements too if you are combining Rwanda with Kenya or Tanzania.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is a golden monkey trekking permit in Rwanda?

A golden monkey trekking permit in Rwanda costs US$100 per foreign adult (checked October 2026 on the RDB booking portal). Foreign residents in Rwanda and East African citizens pay US$65, East African foreign residents pay US$80, and Rwandan citizens pay RWF 4,000. Prices can change, so confirm the current rate before you book.

What is the minimum age for golden monkey trekking?

The minimum age for golden monkey trekking in Rwanda is 12 years, compared with 15 for gorilla trekking. That makes golden monkeys a good choice for families travelling with younger teenagers who cannot yet join a gorilla trek, as long as they can walk for a couple of hours on muddy, uneven ground.

How long does golden monkey trekking take?

Golden monkey trekking usually takes a morning. You report to Kinigi at 07:00 for the briefing, drive to the trailhead and walk into the bamboo zone, and the time you spend with the troop is about one hour. The walk itself depends on where the monkeys moved overnight, so allow the whole morning.

Can you do gorilla and golden monkey trekking on the same day?

Gorilla and golden monkey trekking are normally done on separate days, because both start from Kinigi at 07:00 and the tracking runs once a day. The usual plan is gorillas on day one and golden monkeys the next morning before driving back to Kigali, which needs at least one night near Volcanoes National Park.

Is golden monkey trekking worth it?

Golden monkey trekking is worth it for most travellers already visiting Volcanoes National Park. For US$100 you get an hour with an endangered primate found only in a few highland forests, an easier walk than gorillas and great photo chances. It is especially good value for families and for anyone who cannot do the gorilla trek.

Final Thoughts

Golden monkey trekking in Rwanda gives you an hour with an endangered, playful primate for a US$100 permit, with an easier walk and a lower age limit than gorillas. Add it to a gorilla trek, pair it with Mount Bisoke, or use it as a lower-cost way to see the Virungas.
